question: For about two centuries at a time, the meetings of Jupiter and Saturn fall in the signs of one astrological element. Why?
answer: Because Jupiter goes round about 5 times while Saturn goes round 2. They meet every 20 years, each time two thirds of the way round the sky from the last, so three meetings mark out a triangle. The fit is a little off, so the triangle slowly turns. Kepler drew it in 1596; it is two clocks, not a message.
move: A pattern in the sky is two clocks lining up, not a sign.
ask: Which omens I notice are just two cycles meeting?

scene.caption: Jupiter laps the Sun 5 times while Saturn laps it twice. A line joins them every 30 days.
scene.reveal: Three petals: they meet every 20 years at three points a third of a turn apart.
